_note: The battle royale's match rules that are not the ring's (src/config/ring.json) and not the loot's (src/config/loot.json): how many share a squad, the care package's arrival, the loadout crate and Storm Surge. Apex publishes almost none of this, so nearly every number here says it is ours; the two that are published are cited where they sit.
_teams: Solo, duos and trios, Apex's three squad sizes. `size` is how many share a squad, and the whole lobby plays the host's size. `bots` is the bot counts the lobby row offers, and every one of them is a whole number of bot squads: you, and any friends you bring, are a squad of your own, and nothing fills your squad's empty seats, so a count where 1 + it divided by the size (the first version of this row) left the last bot squad a seat short in every duo and trio lobby. That is the gap item 46 of docs/NEXT_STEPS.md is about, a trio match with holes in it. `bleed` scales the bleed-out clock in src/config/squad.json: a duo has half the time to be picked up because there is only ever one person who can come, and a solo has no bleed-out at all because a knock is the end. Ours: Apex runs the same 90 s in every size.
_defaultTeam: what the lobby opens on, and what a match whose host sent no size (an older build) is
_pod: The care package's arrival (item 32). It used to appear at 120 m with a dim beam, fall in silence and print one line of text. Now it is called first: a notice and a ping name the place it is coming down on, `announce` seconds before it appears, so everyone can start moving. It falls under a canopy trailing smoke, thumps down in a ring of dust, and stays lit and marked for `contest` seconds, which is the window the fight over it happens in. `height` is where it comes in from, unchanged. The fall time itself is loot.json's podFall, which the package already had. `phases` are the ring phases, counted from 0, whose close calls one, and `inset` is how far from the next circle's centre it can land as a fraction of that circle's radius: both were written into the code as rounds 2 to 4 and 0.6 before they came here. Apex announces its packages 4:05 before the ring closes and lands them 2:30 before (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_11.md section 15); ours is that shape scaled to a ten-minute match, and every number below is ours.
_vault: The vault (ours; Apex's vaults open with a vault key found on the map): the small building in the Well's yard, sealed, its one door locked. Its guard, guardName, a bot of guardTier on its own side, stands guardRange metres from the door and fights whoever comes within that; it carries guardGun and the vault keycard, which its death box drops. Whoever holds the keycard opens the vault door with interact, which uses the card. Inside: two supply bins and a mythic gun from the care package's list, at gold mag with every attachment, drawn red. A keycard's holder is shown the way to the vault, a marker renewed every markEvery seconds; a holder who is killed drops it where they fell. Off in Resurgence when its smaller area leaves the Well out.
_podHeard: How far the horn when it is called and the thump when it lands carry, metres, for the page that plays them (src/main.ts, through onRemoteFx). The delay comes for free from the 343 m/s speed of sound the audio already models. Ours.
_podLure: A bot inside this many metres of a package that is falling or still in its contest window goes for it instead of walking its graph. Without this nobody contests a care package but the squad, which is the whole of what makes one an event. Ours.
_loadoutPod: The loadout crate (item 24): the drop that hands you the loadout you built on the Loadouts tab, the way Warzone does it. It comes down in the late rings, one per phase listed, only in a match that lands with nothing (a match that lands with its loadouts has nothing for it to give, which is also when there are no care packages), and it serves the whole lobby: each player claims their own guns out of it once, so a squad mate taking theirs does not empty it. `phases` are the ring's phases counted from 0, so 1 and 4 are the second and the fifth rounds. `after` is how many seconds into its phase's close it is called: the second round's close also calls a care package, both used to be called on the same frame, and the HUD shows one notice at a time, so the package's call was never seen. Eight seconds puts the crate's call between the package's call and its landing, and lands the crate (its announce and the fall after that) before the fifth round's 25 s close is over. The guns arrive kitted to `mag` and `rarity`, fitted by the same code and the same preference list as the Hot Zone's kitted gun (loot.json kitted.prefer), because a second copy of either would drift from the first, and with `stacks` of each one's ammo (ammo.json stacks; an energy gun brings its own stockpile), because a loadout one magazine deep is not one you can fight with. It falls for loot.json's podFall like the care package does. `inset` keeps it well inside the ring it is called into. `claim` is how close you stand, how long you hold still on it, and how far above or below it you can be (so it cannot be claimed through a floor). Ours: Warzone publishes none of this.
_surge: Storm Surge (item 34). The ring only hurts you outside it, so a squad that sits in the middle of the safe zone is never punished and hiding wins ties. From `fromPhase` on, when more players are alive than the phase's share of the lobby allows, everyone is ranked by the damage they have dealt and the ones below the line take a tick of damage wherever they stand, on the ring's own 1.5 s clock. `alive` is that share, one per ring phase: 1 means everyone may live, so the early rounds never surge. `minAlive` is the floor, so the surge never tries to thin a lobby that is already down to a fight. `warn` is the countdown before the first tick, and the surge cancels if enough people die during it. `grace` spares anyone who has dealt damage that recently, because the rule is aimed at hiding and not at losing a fight. `damage` escalates one step every `stepEvery` seconds it stays live. Ours: Apex has not published its thresholds, and ours are fractions of the lobby rather than counts so they hold for a lobby of four as well as one of twelve.
_console: Ring Consoles (src/game/ringconsole.ts): `count` terminals, each near one of the map's places, between `near` and `far` metres from its middle on clear ground. Hold the interact key for `hold` seconds within `reach` metres and the circle after next goes on the whole squad's map, dashed, until the ring gets there; the console is spent until the ring closes, and the scan pays `evo`. Apex gives the scan to one class of legend and does not publish its numbers; these are ours. The hold is the NEXT_STEPS item's 7.5 s, long enough that a scan in the open is a risk.
_resurgence: Resurgence (src/game/resurgence.ts), Warzone's rules over this battle royale. While they are on, the dead redeploy from the sky after redeploy[round] seconds (15 early and 39 late, the NEXT_STEPS item's numbers); each knock by your side takes knockCut and each kill killCut off the wait of everyone of yours who is dead, never below `floor`. A side whose every member is down or dead at once is out. From ring round endPhase + 1 every death is final; a wait already running then still finishes. The ring's waits and closes run at ringScale of the battle royale's, the circles and damage the same. A redeploy lands you 8 to `spread` metres from a squad mate who is up, or alone somewhere inside the ring, and in a match that lands with nothing it comes with one of `kit`, kitStacks stacks of its ammo and the heals in `heals`. Ours, except the 15 and 39.

resurgence._area: Resurgence is played on a quarter of Outskirts, as Apex plays it on a part of a map: the first circle is radius metres across the hub, leaning lean metres toward one of the four big places round it (from the match seed), which takes in the hub, that place and the two compounds beside it. The squad and the bots drop on places inside it, and every round's circle shrinks with it.

_gulag: The Gulag (src/game/gulag.ts), under the battle royale's own rules (Resurgence has its redeploys instead). A first death before ring round untilPhase + 1 sends you, `delay` seconds later, to the arena `map` against a bot of tier `tier`, the two of you on two of `guns` drawn for the fight; a countdown of `countdown` seconds, then `fight` seconds, then overtime: a flag `flagRadius` metres across in the room's middle, won by `capture` seconds on it alone. Win and you drop back into the match `after` seconds later with those guns and kitStacks stacks of their ammo; lose and you are out. One trip a match. Ours: Warzone's Gulag is the idea, and none of its numbers carry over to a map this size.
